planting.note: Set out well-rooted plants after all danger of frost has passed, once nights stay reliably warm.

directions: Foliage emerges deep purple to near black, giving an upright plant dramatic contrast against lighter companions. Grows as a tall, well-branched thriller equally at home in full sun or shade. Pinch stray flower spikes to keep energy focused on foliage. Feed and water regularly through summer heat for continuous dense color.

planting.note: Plant out after frost danger has passed and soil has warmed.

directions: Feathery, finely cut maroon-red leaves are heavily flecked with chartreuse speckles, with red tones deepening in shadier spots. Quickly fills out into a robust, upright mass suited to mass plantings and borders. Tolerates both sun and shade and rarely flowers, keeping foliage fresh into fall. Water and feed regularly for best color saturation.

planting.note: Set out after frost risk has passed; works well in hanging baskets and mixed containers.

directions: Green leaves are marked with red venation and a bright red-and-yellow center, giving a multicolored, pink-and-white accented look. Habit is trailing and mounded, cascading up to two feet, making it a strong spiller for containers and baskets. Performs well from full sun to full shade and is deer resistant. Pinch any flower spikes to maintain foliage density.

planting.note: Plant out once nights are warm and frost danger has passed.

directions: Vivid orange foliage with a ruffled leaf edge covers a densely branched, upright plant that fills out without becoming leggy. Thrives in full sun or partial shade, holding color well in both. Blooms late if at all, so foliage stays showy through most of the season. Grows tall enough to use as a thriller in large containers or as a landscape border accent.

planting.note: Set out after frost danger passes; ideal for hanging baskets and container edges.

directions: Small, intensely colored leaves show red venation with a bright red-and-yellow center and lime-green edges. Rather than growing upright, this type mounds and trails over container rims, forming a dense cascading mass. Retains its vivid coloring in both sun and shade and rarely blooms, keeping color consistent until frost. Use as a low-maintenance spiller in mixed plantings.

planting.note: Plant out after frost danger passes; a compact choice for small containers and border edges.

directions: Compact, well-branched mounds carry watermelon-to-coral foliage brushed with golden chartreuse accents, occasionally showing darker burgundy sections that can be pinched out. Noticeably smaller than standard ColorBlaze types, making it well suited to borders and small containers. Tolerates sun or shade but colors best and resists bleaching in shadier spots. Blooms very late if at all, keeping foliage the main attraction.

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; useful for window boxes and small-space plantings.

directions: Bright golden chartreuse foliage covers a densely branched, compact mound, delivering strong color in a small footprint. Grows well in either full sun or full shade, offering flexibility across garden spots. Flowers very late in the season if at all, so foliage quality holds through fall. Works well massed in borders or tucked into window boxes and upright containers.
